changelog: Three additions from Joshua's live use on 2026-10-18. (1) THE BUILDING NOW TRAVELS WITH THE STREET JUMP: in the 3D view, clicking a street and jumping to the Map Editor used to send only the street — Joshua landed in the Map Editor zoomed to the road with no idea where his building was supposed to go, because the building was never sent. Now, when a building is open in the 3D view, the handoff also carries the building: its name, its zone, its ground outline exactly as the editor holds it (drags included), and its centre point. The Map Editor (1.9.8 and later) draws it there and selects the street it fronts. A jump with no building open — and a jump from a gas station — writes exactly the same handoff as before. (2) THE CORNER PROGRESS BAR (the progress-bar law): like the Map Editor's, a small progress bar now sits in the bottom-right corner, at the end of the status bar, whenever the app is working in the background — downloading, fetching a building's details, opening a station, or saving to GitHub. It shows real progress when a total is known and keeps moving when it isn't, so a busy app never looks frozen; it clears when the work is done. The existing download readout in MB stays where it was. (3) UNIVERSAL VIEWPORT CONTROLS in the 3D view — the one scheme Joshua set for every viewport in the suite: click-and-hold drag pans the view, the mouse wheel zooms, the + and − keys zoom the same way, and Ctrl+drag rotates. Dragging the building itself (roof to move, an edge to resize, the orange front wall for height) and clicking a street to select it work exactly as before, and the Face front button resets the whole view — position, zoom and angle.
